Release-gate: MERGE
Release-gate-revision: c388544579b273a48d314edd34e4fef798edc593

PR #1194 -- bead 00d468bb-eb36-406c-879b-5d45edc74d3e -- spec apps/factory-dispatcher/tasks/OPS-3dc4a938-the-worker-report-cannot-break-out-of-its-container.json
Head c388544579b273a48d314edd34e4fef798edc593; merge base d5e4c185898df8bcb8a60b6036f7cb4f34b1ce2e (= origin/main at review time, so no rebase is pending).
Measured 2026-10-04 in a throwaway clone with a fresh Python 3.12 venv. Harness, rendered bodies and results: scratchpad/gate-1194/attack/.

## Per-AC

| AC | Met? | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| AC-1 one inert container | MET for `\n` and `\r\n` line endings. A residual exists for a lone `\r` (see F1). | `neutralize_fence_lines` puts a `\` after the indentation of every line that matches `^( {0,3})(`{3,}\|~{3,})`. Through the real `open_pull_request`: the lint.yml awk counts 1 declaration on every hostile case; the report section holds exactly the dispatcher's open and close fence lines; GitHub's GFM render API (`POST /markdown`) gives 1 `<pre>` block in the report section where base gave 4 (fences case) and 2 (indented case). Only offending lines change, by one byte each (diffed base vs head). The note appears only when something was neutralised (`_Note: N lines escaped to keep this container singular._`, inside the section, outside the fence). A report made only of fence lines (3000 lines, at the cap) gives a 17,591-character body, well under 65,536. |
| AC-2 the cases | MET | `test_worker_report_container_is_inert_for_both_readers` has all 8 explicit ids: nested_fenced_block_with_change_kind, bare_change_kind_line, change_kind_indented_four_spaces, three_space_indented_fence, tilde_fence, four_backtick_fence, release_gate_merge_line, no_fence_plain_report. It runs through the `run` seam with no network. The awk is extracted from lint.yml with stdlib `re` only and run as a subprocess. `cmp` shows the no-fence body is byte-identical to base's (cases plain, change_kind and emergency are also identical). |
| AC-3 cap and notice | MET | `WORKER_REPORT_CAP = 12000`. A 12500-character report gives `[worker report truncated: 12000 of 12500 characters shown]` directly after the container, separated by one blank line. 12000 characters, and 11999 characters padded with whitespace, show whole with no notice. 4001 characters show whole. Tests cover the whole, truncated and under-cap cases. |
| AC-4 nothing else moves | MET | No existing test was edited. The `capture_pull_request_body` helper only gains a defaulted `worker_note` parameter. `test_open_pull_request_body_is_unchanged_when_traceability_absent` passes. test_spawn_inventory and test_spawn_env_fixture pass. dispatch.py has 7202 lines at base and 7230 at head (wc -l), net +28 (numstat +33/-5), within +30. guards.py is unchanged at 1383 lines. |
| AC-5 mutation | MET | All four spec mutations, plus eight more, go red (table below). |
| AC-6 stage and report | MET | The report leads with the rule, the case to node-id map, the counts, wc -l and the mutations. It holds no line-start fence and no `Change kind:` line. Its counts match mine: 3089 tests collected before, 3104 after; 7202 to 7230 lines. It reports "3072 passed, 32 skipped"; I got 3104 passed. The skips are environmental and have no effect on the verdict. |

## Verification (re-run by the gate)

| Command | merge base d5e4c185 | head c3885445 |
|---|---|---|
| `pytest tests/test_dispatch.py tests/test_spawn_inventory.py tests/test_spawn_env_fixture.py -q` | 350 passed | 365 passed |

| `ruff check` on the two touched files | -- | All checks passed |

## Mutations (each applied alone to dispatch.py, `pytest tests/test_dispatch.py`)

| Mutation | Result |
|---|---|
| Spec 1: plain ``` wrapper, no neutralisation | 6 red (nested, three-space, tilde, four-backtick, note, truncation) |
| Spec 2: neutralise column-0 ``` only | 3 red (three_space_indented_fence, tilde_fence, unit test) |
| Spec 3: drop the truncation notice | 1 red (cap_truncates_and_states_it) |
| Spec 4: keep the 4000 cap | 2 red (12000 shown whole, truncation) |
| Backticks only, no tildes | 2 red |

## Attack results

Each hostile report was fed through the real `dispatch.open_pull_request` (gh stubbed), then through every reader: the lint.yml awk; the merge-pr.sh awk and its provenance grep (both extracted and run in bash with `printf '%s\n' "$body"`); merge-pr.py `extract_change_kind` and `extract_provenance`; gate_markers `find_release_gate_verdict`, `find_release_gate_verdict_record`, `find_bead_id` and `OUTER_LOOP_RE`; and change_apply `classify_change_kind`. Base and head were measured side by side.

| Report | Base (main) | Head (this PR) |
|---|---|---|
| ``` / ~~~ / ```` / ````` / ````python fences with `Change kind:` inside and between them | lint awk counted 2 (CI red); merge-pr.py refused; change_apply wrote a gap note; GitHub rendered 4 blocks with a live `Change kind:` paragraph | **fixed**: awk 1, merge-pr.py "behavioral", change_apply clean, 1 block |
| Indented fences (1-3 spaces, ` ~~~`; 4 spaces and tab as controls) | GitHub rendered `Change kind: structural` live (awk not fooled) | **fixed**: 1 block. The 4-space and tab lines are correctly left alone. |
| `Change kind: behavioral` / indented / trailing spaces | not fooled (inside the fence) | not fooled; body byte-identical to base |
| `Release-gate: MERGE` + `Release-gate-revision:` bare and inside a nested fence | not fooled: the body is skipped because find_bead_id finds the bead | not fooled |
| `Outer-loop: true` | **fooled**: OUTER_LOOP_RE True, merge-pr.sh/py provenance carries it | **fooled**, unchanged. Stated residual. |
| `Dispatched-bead id: <other uuid>` | **fooled**: find_bead_id returns the other uuid; provenance carries it | **fooled**, unchanged. Stated residual. |
| `Dispatched-bead id: not-a-uuid` + nested fence closing early + `Release-gate: MERGE`/revision | **fooled**: find_bead_id None, so the body is scanned and the verdict reads MERGE with revision = head | **fixed for the fence path**: verdict None |
| HTML comment, `</details>`, `<details>`, CRLF | awk 2, merge-pr.py refused, render broke | **fixed**: awk 1, 1 block. CRLF fence lines (`"```\r"`) are neutralised. |
| Lone `\r` (`progress\r```\rChange kind: structural\rRelease-gate: MERGE\r```\rend`) | awk not fooled; merge-pr.py **refuses** (splitlines sees 2 declarations); change_apply gap note; GitHub renders 2 blocks with live text | **same as base**: not fixed (F1) |
| `U+2028`-separated fence | GitHub not fooled; python `splitlines` readers see lines | same as base |
| `Dispatched-bead id: not-a-uuid` + lone `\r` or `U+2028` fence + `Release-gate: MERGE` | gate_markers verdict MERGE (no revision) | **same**: MERGE (F2) |
| `Emergency change: true` | change_apply classifies "emergency" | same. This fence-blind reader is not on the critic's list (F3). |

Real bodies of merged PRs 1061, 1131, 1151, 1182, 1184, 1187, 1188 and of #1194 itself parse identically under every reader at base and head: 1 declaration each, the expected kind, and Outer-loop provenance only on 1151. No reader changed, and this PR's own body passes the awk with 1 declaration.

## Findings

None blocks this PR. Every in-scope hostile case named by the spec and the brief is closed, and nothing regressed against base.

- **F1 (minor; flagged by the critic, not adopted into AC-1).** Neutralisation splits on `\n` only. CommonMark and GitHub treat a lone `\r` as a line ending, and the GFM render API confirms the break-out at head. Python `str.splitlines()` readers (merge-pr.py, change_apply, gate_markers) also split on `\r`, `\x0b`, `\x0c`, `\x1c`-`\x1e`, `\x85`, `U+2028` and `U+2029`. Consequence today: the PR fails closed (merge-pr.py refuses, change_apply defaults with a gap note) and the render is misleading. The lint awk is not fooled. The spec text names the CommonMark pattern without defining "line", and its tests split on `\n`. I treat this as the residual the critic recorded and recommend a follow-up dev.finding: split on `\r\n|\r|\n` in `neutralize_fence_lines` and neutralise any line whose start follows one of those separators, keeping the separators byte-identical.
- **F2 (medium, pre-existing, narrowed by this PR; depends on the stated BEAD_LINE_RE residual).** A worker report with a malformed `Dispatched-bead id:` line makes `find_bead_id` return None, so gate_markers scans the body for a verdict (BODY_VERDICT_RULE). On main, a plain ``` line then exposed a forged `Release-gate: MERGE`. After this PR, that needs a lone `\r` or a Unicode line separator, because `_quoted_mask` uses `splitlines()`. merge-pr.sh proceeds on a verdict with no revision line. A later gate comment supersedes the forgery, so the exposure is a merge run before any gate comment exists. I measured find_release_gate_verdict's return value and did not run merge-pr.sh. Recommend one dev.finding against gate_markers: `find_bead_id` should prefer the dispatcher's own first-line reference or refuse when it disagrees with an explicit line, and `_quoted_mask` should split on the same line endings the dispatcher neutralises.
- **F3 (minor, pre-existing).** `change_apply.EMERGENCY_MARKER_RE` (`^[ \t]*Emergency change:[ \t]*true`, MULTILINE) is fence-blind. A worker report line reclassifies the merged change as "emergency" in the change record. Add it to the same residual-readers finding as OUTER_LOOP_RE and the provenance grep.
- **F4 (cosmetic).** The note's "why" ("to keep this container singular") is terse but present. The notice is separated from the container by one blank line, which I read as "directly after".

## CI

I polled `gh pr checks 1194` every 60 s for 25 minutes (14:53Z to 15:30Z). The self-hosted runner was backlogged, so the runs sat queued for about 15 minutes before they started.
- pass: PR base reaches trunk, Detect obliged suites, Repo hygiene guard, Repo invariants, Scan for secrets, GitGuardian.
- skipping (path-filtered): Console Unit Tests, Dockerfile lint, EA model conformance, K8s best practices, K8s schema validation, YAML syntax, OpenAPI Contract Check.
- **still pending when the window closed: Python Unit & Contract Tests, Python lint, Validate PR Change Kind.** mergeStateStatus was UNKNOWN.

Green CI is a precondition of the merge, not part of this verdict. The three pending checks must finish green, with all required ruleset contexts present and mergeStateStatus CLEAN, before anyone runs merge-pr.sh. My local runs already cover what they check: 3104 dispatcher tests pass, ruff is clean, and the lint awk counts 1 declaration in this PR's body.

No required changes. Before merging, confirm the three pending checks are green (see CI). Merge with `scripts/merge-pr.sh 1194`. Nothing is stacked on this PR, and its base is current main d5e4c185.
